LanguageData.MeleeWeapon_Dao.label: dao
LanguageData.MeleeWeapon_Dao.description: Dao are single-edged Chinese swords, primarily used for slashing and chopping.
LanguageData.MeleeWeapon_Dao.tools.handle.label: handle
LanguageData.MeleeWeapon_Dao.tools.point.label: point
LanguageData.MeleeWeapon_Dao.tools.edge.label: edge
LanguageData.MeleeWeapon_FengHuoLun.label: Feng-Huo-Lun
LanguageData.MeleeWeapon_FengHuoLun.description: Feng-huo-lun, or Wind-and-fire wheels, are melee weapons, wielded as a pair, associated with Chinese martial arts such as baguazhang and taijiquan. Visually, they are similar to chakrams.
LanguageData.MeleeWeapon_FengHuoLun.tools.edge.label: edge
LanguageData.MeleeWeapon_Jian.label: jian
LanguageData.MeleeWeapon_Jian.description: The jian is a double-edged straight sword used during the last 2,500 years in China.
LanguageData.MeleeWeapon_Jian.tools.handle.label: handle
LanguageData.MeleeWeapon_Jian.tools.point.label: point
LanguageData.MeleeWeapon_Jian.tools.edge.label: edge
LanguageData.MeleeWeapon_Kabutowari.label: kabutowari
LanguageData.MeleeWeapon_Kabutowari.description: The Kabutowari also known as hachiwari, was a type of knife-shaped weapon, resembling a jitte in many respects. This weapon was carried as a side-arm by the samurai class of feudal Japan.
LanguageData.MeleeWeapon_Kabutowari.tools.blade.label: blade
LanguageData.MeleeWeapon_Kabutowari.tools.point.label: point
LanguageData.MeleeWeapon_Kanabo.label: kanabo
LanguageData.MeleeWeapon_Kanabo.description: The kanabo was a spiked or knobbed club or truncheon used in feudal Japan as a weapon by samurai and their retainers.
LanguageData.MeleeWeapon_Kanabo.tools.handle.label: handle
LanguageData.MeleeWeapon_Kanabo.tools.head.label: head
LanguageData.MeleeWeapon_Katana.label: katana
LanguageData.MeleeWeapon_Katana.description: katana were one of the traditionally made Japanese swords that were used by the samurai of feudal Japan.
LanguageData.MeleeWeapon_Katana.tools.handle.label: handle
LanguageData.MeleeWeapon_Katana.tools.edge.label: edge
LanguageData.MeleeWeapon_MonkSpade.label: monk's spade
LanguageData.MeleeWeapon_MonkSpade.description: A monk's spade, also called a Shaolin Spade, is a Chinese pole weapon consisting of a long pole with a flat spade-like blade on one end and a smaller crescent shaped blade on the other. Neither blade was designed to be sharpened.
LanguageData.MeleeWeapon_MonkSpade.tools.handle.label: handle
LanguageData.MeleeWeapon_MonkSpade.tools.head.label: head
LanguageData.MeleeWeapon_Naginata.label: naginata
LanguageData.MeleeWeapon_Naginata.description: The naginata is one of several varieties of traditionally made Japanese blades in the form of a pole weapon. Naginata were originally used by the samurai class of feudal Japan, as well as by ashigaru (foot soldiers) and sohei (warrior monks).
LanguageData.MeleeWeapon_Naginata.tools.handle.label: handle
LanguageData.MeleeWeapon_Naginata.tools.head.label: head
LanguageData.MeleeWeapon_Naginata.tools.edge.label: edge
LanguageData.MeleeWeapon_Ninjato.label: ninjato
LanguageData.MeleeWeapon_Ninjato.description: The ninjato are allegedly the preferred weapon that the Shinobi of feudal Japan carried.
LanguageData.MeleeWeapon_Ninjato.tools.handle.label: handle
LanguageData.MeleeWeapon_Ninjato.tools.blade.label: blade
LanguageData.MeleeWeapon_Ninjato.tools.point.label: point
LanguageData.MeleeWeapon_Yari.label: yari
LanguageData.MeleeWeapon_Yari.description: Yari is the term for one of the traditionally made Japanese blades in the form of a spear.
LanguageData.MeleeWeapon_Yari.tools.handle.label: handle
LanguageData.MeleeWeapon_Yari.tools.head.label: head
LanguageData.MeleeWeapon_Yari.tools.edge.label: edge
